newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Shoes, OJ and airplanes boost Brazil exports.
newsitem.headline: Shoes, OJ and airplanes boost Brazil exports.

text.p: Exports of shoes, orange juice and airplanes stood out in Brazil's overseas sales for November, said Mauricio Cortes, foreign trade secretary at the Ministry of Industry and Commerce.

Cortes said transport materials, principally sales of aircraft to France and the United States, led the way, expanding 11.03 percent over October, with exports of $453 million. Exports of orange juice hit $123 million, down from $144 million in October, but up from $96 million in November 1995, and leather shoe sales were $201 million versus $199 million in October and $163 million last November.
"Primary and manufactured goods stood out, mainly orange juice, shoes and transport material," Cortes told reporters.

On the downside, lower metal product prices this year meant lower dollar-value exports of those items and the late harvest last year of soybeans meant this November's soybean shipments showed a 37 percent fall year-on-year.
Metal product exports in November this year were 34 percent down at $417 million versus $634 million and soybean shipments slumped to $218 million from $348 million in November 1995.
